ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a bar chart of the breeding season, with the vertical axis as the mean testosterone level (Mean T level), and the horizontal axis comparing “Helper male” and “Breeding male”. The bar heights of the two types of males are almost the same, both around about 50, indicating that the so-called helper males have testosterone levels in the breeding season as high as those of breeding males. The question states that these data come from different years of the same population, so this same high testosterone level can be used as evidence for judging their role. Since high breeding-season testosterone levels are consistent with breeding behavior, the so-called “helper males” are not merely helpers, but are actually also breeding.
